## Summary

The Terminal Configuration object controls reader settings such as splash screens, tipping and offline mode. The May 1, 2026 capture contains a combined Dashboard and API guide. The November 7 capture provides links to the two variants.

## Configuration Hierarchy (May 2026)

Stripe provisions an account default for the fleet. A Location configuration overrides individual settings for readers there, and every setting without a Location override inherits the account default. The default cannot be applied directly to a Location. May describes zone configuration as a private preview. Dashboard or API changes could take up to ten minutes to reach target readers in the May guide.

## Dashboard Operations (May 2026)

Use **Manage locations** to edit the account’s default configuration or create, edit and delete a local configuration. The May **Delete an existing configuration** workflow says deleting a local configuration through the Dashboard returns that Location’s readers to their account defaults within ten minutes (May raw lines 81–94).

## API Operations (May 2026)

- **Account default lookup.** The prose links to Retrieve, but the worked example calls `configurations.list({ is_account_default: true })`. The separate November List reference documents the optional `is_account_default` filter. The Retrieve reference describes retrieval of a single Configuration object. See May raw lines 100–112 and the November List reference lines 41–42.
- **Create and assign.** The example creates a Configuration and sets the object ID in the Location’s `configuration_overrides` using `locations.update`. See May raw lines 114–143.
- **Update and delete.** The May API variant gives separate `configurations.update` and `configurations.del` operations. The separate November API Delete reference documents deletion of one Configuration, with reader fallback timing left unspecified. See May raw lines 145–174 and the November Delete reference lines 5–7 and 24–41.

terminal-fleet-configurations-overview.text: Use the Terminal Configurations object to apply configurations to your readers.
You can override account-level settings with location-level settings.
Any configuration changes made with the API or Dashboard can take up to 10 minutes to reflect on the target readers.
After you delete the configuration, the readers in the location default back to the account’s default configuration within 10 minutes.
You can’t apply the default configuration directly to a Location.

terminal-fleet-configurations-overview.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/configurations-overview, the November 7, 2026 capture states that the Terminal Configurations object applies reader settings and routes implementers to Dashboard or API variants. It carries no documented setup prerequisites or state transitions itself (new raw lines 5-14). The May 1, 2026 capture documents the account/location hierarchy for splash screen, tipping and offline mode. Stripe provisions account defaults; a fleet operator can override per location; the readers inherit settings without an override and cannot receive the account default through direct location assignment. API/Dashboard changes can take up to 10 minutes and zone configuration was private preview (old raw lines 8-26 and old raw lines 100-112). The Dashboard operator can update account settings, create or change a location configuration, or delete local configuration, with the last action reverting readers to account defaults within 10 minutes (old raw lines 32-61 and old raw lines 63-94). An API integration lists account defaults using the filter, creates a Configuration and associates it via locations.update's configuration_overrides, or updates/deletes a Configuration (old raw lines 100-130 and old raw lines 137-174). The original source covered the hierarchy and examples. The revised source-stripe-terminal-configurations.md separates Dashboard default editing and local deletion from the API operations.
terminal-fleet-configurations-overview.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/configurations-overview, source-stripe-terminal-configurations.md retains the May 1, 2026 functional capture and adds the November 7, 2026 capture as dated navigation. The latter's Dashboard and API destinations are navigation only. The disappearance of full sections from the base capture documents a presentation/capture-scope change without proving any feature removal, preview or rollout change (new raw lines 9-14, old raw lines 28-41 and old raw lines 96-112). Keep the dated May account/default/override inheritance boundaries, up-to propagation, and zone preview (new raw lines 5-14, old raw lines 8-26 and old raw line 102). The revised Dashboard wording distinguishes editing the default from creating, updating and deleting local configuration. The account-default fallback and 10-minute wording apply to the documented Dashboard local deletion, with the API deletion described separately (old raw lines 34-61 and old raw lines 81-94 and old raw lines 164-174). The prior account-default lookup prose links to Retrieve, but the example uses List with is_account_default=true (old raw lines 100-112); preserve the documented List filter and route single-object lookup separately. The proposed reciprocal stripe-terminal-hardware-orders route dates the preview and timing attributions. Its API paragraph keeps API deletion separate and links the default fallback to the May Dashboard local-deletion steps (old raw lines 81-94). The independent API passages describe deletion without specifying a reader fallback (old raw lines 164-174 and raw/stripe-api-terminal-configuration-delete-2026-11-07.md:5-7 and :24-41).

concept_suggestions.anchor: Locations inherit account defaults unless overridden. Changes propagate within **10 minutes**. Zone-level configurations are in private preview.
